**Claim 0: R-134a boils at about minus 26 degrees Celsius at normal air pressure**
- The Engineering Mindset property table: R-134a (CH2FCF3), used in domestic refrigeration and car air conditioners, boiling point -26.3 °C (-15.34 °F) at atmospheric pressure. URL: https://theengineeringmindset.com/thermodynamic-properties-refrigerant-r-134a/
- Hudson Technologies R-134a PT chart: boiling point (1 atm) -14.9 °F (about -26.1 °C). URL: https://www.hudsontech.com/pdfs/pt-charts/R-134a-Pressure-Temperature-Chart.pdf
- Verdict: supported as written (about -26 °C).

**Claim 1: Food safety agencies say a fridge should be at 4 °C (40 F) or colder**
- FDA consumer update (archived): "Keep the refrigerator temperature at or below 40° F (4° C). The freezer temperature should be 0° F (-18° C)." It ties the limit to Listeria growth. URL: https://webarchive.library.unt.edu/web/20080916171410/http://www.fda.gov/consumer/updates/foodstorage072108.html
- FDA health educators page (archived 2012) gives the same 40 °F limit. URL: https://webarchive.library.unt.edu/web/20121020003248/http://www.fda.gov/Food/ResourcesForYou/HealthEducators/ucm083063.htm
- Verdict: supported as written.

**Claim 2: A fridge does not make cold; it moves heat from inside the box to the coils outside**
- Sears Home Services: the refrigerator removes heat from the food inside and releases it into the kitchen through the condenser coils at the back or bottom. URL: https://www.searshomeservices.com/blog/how-does-a-refrigerator-work
- LibreTexts HVAC course (Condenser): the condenser rejects the heat absorbed by the refrigerant to the surrounding air, condensing it to a liquid. URL: https://workforce.libretexts.org/Courses/Coalinga_College/Introduction_to_Residential_HVAC_Level_1/03%3A_Introduction_to_Cooling_Systems-_Air_Conditioning_and_Refrigeration/3.03%3A_Components_of_Cooling_Systems/3.3.02%3A_Condenser
- Verdict: supported as written.
